elements.text: AZT – zidovudine; DTG – dolutegravir; FTC – emtricitabine; TDF – tenofovir; 3TC – lamivudine; HBsAg – Hepatitis B surface antigen; HBsAbs – Hepatitis B surface antibody
HIV: POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (PEP)
Body fluids transmit infection through sexual exposure (rape/sexual assault or consensual sex, burst condom), occupational or non-occupational exposure (sharps injury, splash to eye, mouth, nose or
broken skin), sharing needles, contact with used condom and exposure to blood. Tears, saliva (non-bloodstained), sweat, urine and stool are considered non-infectious fluids.

1Advise patient on possible side effects of HIV PEP and to return promptly if they occur. Advise condom use. 2If dolutegravir not tolerated or contraindicated, give instead atazanavir 300mg + ritonavir 100mg once daily or lopinavir 400mg + ritonavir 100mg 12 hourly. 3If giving both hepatitis B vaccine and immunoglobulin, give at different sites.
